frontend: CrabEmu 0.2.0 for Mac OS X (the official 2013 universal app, its x86_64 slice under Rosetta 2), isolated with CFFIXED_USER_HOME
options: -SMSDomestic NO on the command line (export console; the app's default is the Japanese one)
input: work/standalone/crabemu/crabfeed.c, loaded with DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES (the binary is unsigned): one frame per call of the emulation thread's semaphore_wait on the app's sound semaphore; the retro-run script's buttons written into sms_pad (b = button 1, a = button 2), start = Pause via sms_z80_nmi(), reset = sms_soft_reset() (what the app's Reset menu item calls); the ROM opened through the app delegate's application:openFiles:; [NSApp terminate:] at the end. NSUserDefaults writes and the recent-documents list were stubbed out so nothing reached the owner's preferences. proof.png is the app's own framebuffer (ARGB1555), dumped at the script's last shot

layout.save_dir: Library/Application Support/ljsdcdev/CrabEmu/SRAM Saves in the home folder (preference SaveDirectory)
layout.name: <ROM file name, extension included>.ces
layout.content: the cartridge RAM buffer, always 32768 bytes, 0x00 past what the game uses (a 93C46 EEPROM game would get 128 bytes)
layout.written: when the app quits or closes the ROM, only if the game enabled cartridge RAM

note: Played with Monopoly.sms-plus-gx.txt: CrabEmu powers cartridge RAM on as zeros, which Monopoly takes for a saved game (the shared script reached GAME RESTORED instead; not filed), as in picodrive and sms-plus-gx. The file differs from every other core in about 5400 of the first 8192 bytes: many fields hold 0xF0 where the others hold 0x00. CrabEmu fills the console's 8 KiB work RAM with 0xF0 at power-on (smsmem.c), and Monopoly copies uninitialised work RAM into its save.
